reason: At base, REGEX_FORMAT matches Y{1,4} but format() only implements YY and YYYY, so lone 'Y' and 'YYY' fall through to the timezone-offset fallback and produce offset-like output instead of the expected literal 'Y' and two-digit-year+'Y'.

After the fix, REGEX_FORMAT only matches YYYY|YY, so unsupported 'Y' tokens pass through literally: format('Y') returns 'Y' and format('YYY') returns the two-digit year followed by a literal 'Y', matching the expectation.
At base the request already decodes param values containing '%' via tryDecode(decodeURIComponent_), so a %20 in a route parameter is decoded to a space before the refactor.
The refactor only extracts the identical 'contains % then decode' logic into a shared tryDecodeURIComponent utility, so percent-encoded route parameters are still decoded the same way.
At base, SortedEntry#reschedule only performs the zincrby and never updates @score, so the same in-memory entry keeps reporting the stale pre-reschedule score and time.
The fix sets @score = at.to_f after the zincrby, so the held entry's score and at immediately reflect the newly requested reschedule time.
The PR only changes Range header parsing (parseRangesSpecifier); Content-Type parsing is untouched, and 'text/plain; charset=UTF-8' parses correctly with charset UTF-8 at base.
Content-Type parsing is unaffected by the Range whitespace change, so the header still parses to text/plain with charset UTF-8 at head.

The logging-only PR does not touch archiving, and Composer's zip archiver adds files via ZipArchive::addFile which preserves source file modification times, so extracted files keep their original release-date timestamps.
The PR is unrelated to archiving; re-archiving the same package still records source-matching modification times in the zip on both revisions, with no 1980-01-01 defaults.
The CredentialCache prefix-path PR does not touch System.Text.Json, and DeserializeAsync of a List<T> whose element type has a nullable parent property completes without throwing at this revision.
The PR is unrelated to JSON serialization; both synchronous and asynchronous deserialization of the same payload succeed and produce equivalent object graphs.
The cursor FETCH FIRST fix does not touch INET operators, and CockroachDB supports <<= with ANY, returning true since 192.168.1.5 is contained in 192.168.1.0/24.
The PR is unrelated to INET; >>= ANY over an INET array parses without a syntax error and returns true because 10.0.0.0/8 contains 10.1.2.3.
At base every NO_PROXY entry is mounted as 'all://*<hostname>', so '::1' becomes the unparseable pattern 'all://*::1' and constructing the client raises an error.
The fix classifies '::1' as IPv6 and mounts it as 'all://[::1]', a valid pattern, so client construction succeeds and requests to other hosts proceed normally.
At base the flag round-trip in Series.str.match only preserves re.IGNORECASE, so passing re.DOTALL via flags= or a compiled pattern raises instead of matching 'a\nc'.
The fix restores support for non-IGNORECASE flags, so with DOTALL enabled 'a\nc' matches 'a.c' and 'ac' does not, both via flags= and via a pre-compiled pattern.

At base, prepare_steps leaves prev_task/prev_res stale after upgrading a mid-chain group to a chord, so result wiring for chains containing groups is broken and the serialization round-trip does not preserve all group children.
The fix updates prev_task/prev_res after each chord upgrade, so a chain with two mid-chain groups freezes and serializes correctly and all four group child results survive reconstruction.

The PR only fixes the case where -- is the very first argument; when values precede --, the first positional's value_terminator already stops collection mid-list and hands the remaining arguments to the second positional at base.
At head the mid-list -- is still handled by the first positional's value terminator, leaving value1/value2 in it and letting the second positional collect --check, so parsing succeeds.
At base a post-startup OSC 11 response sets 'background' via nvim_set_option_value, which fires OptionSet after startup and re-triggers ColorScheme on the background change, as the test expects.
The fix sets background with :noautocmd specifically to suppress the OptionSet event (and ColorScheme is suppressed with it), so the autocommands the test expects no longer fire at head.
The PR only reorders compile-time @derive handling in Ecto.Schema; changeset casting plus validate_required still reports the changeset invalid with a "can't be blank" error for the omitted field.
Required-field validation is untouched by the derive compile-time dependency change, so the changeset is still invalid with a "can't be blank" error at head.
